blocks.rationale: Create a generic OpenExempt formatter that reads a flat, current-source claim record, preserves exact asset descriptions and literal citations, and emits either native EC or EV output. This targets the Illinois trigger while remaining applicable to prior Federal/Wisconsin cases instead of hard-coding one jurisdiction or asset list.

inputs.name: asset_names
inputs.question: What are the exact asset descriptions appearing in the current Facts, without ownership or valuation wording?

inputs.name: asset_values
inputs.question: What dollar value belongs to each current asset in the same order?

inputs.name: claim_asset_indexes
inputs.question: For every exemption applicable under the already-determined governing exemption systems, what zero-based current-asset index does the claim concern? Repeat an index when multiple exemptions apply.

inputs.name: claim_citations
inputs.question: In the same order, what literal statutory citation string identifies each applicable exemption? Include only the specific exemption citations required by the current output contract, not enabling or definitional provisions.

inputs.name: claim_limits
inputs.question: In the same order, what maximum dollar amount can be protected for each asset-exemption pair when considered independently under the current contract? For an unlimited exemption, use the corresponding asset's full value.

inputs.name: output_family
inputs.question: Does the current response schema require citation arrays (EC) or citation-and-claim-value records (EV)?

skill.intent: Build the native EC or EV asset-exemption mapping from current-source asset facts and independently assessed applicable exemption claims.

outputs.description: The complete native asset-keyed EC or EV exemption mapping.
outputs.name: answer

reads.question: Read the current governing exemption systems, Facts, and response contract to identify the assets and all independently applicable exemption claims as aligned flat arrays.
reads.source_locator: current OpenExempt statutes, solved governing-law step, Facts, and output contract

origin.quote: The Debtor may claim property exemptions under Illinois statutes.

source_obligations.statement: Use only exemptions available under the governing exemption systems identified in the current solved reasoning step.

origin.quote: Consider each asset-exemption pair independently, without factoring in aggregate values across multiple assets.

source_obligations.statement: For EV output, assess each asset-exemption pair independently and cap the claim at the lesser of the asset value and the exemption's applicable dollar limit.

The personal property exemptions set forth in this Section shall apply only to individuals and only to personal property that is used for personal rather than business purposes.

blocks.rationale: Create an airline terminal helper around one coupled per-item assessment. Parallel arrays retain bag order and force the source reader to account for carried-item allowances, complimentary checked bags, checked ordinals, route, cabin, weight allowance, and size band before deterministic aggregation.

inputs.name: ticket_price
inputs.question: What integer ticket price is stated for the current passenger?

inputs.name: bag_base_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in stated order, what base checked-bag fee applies after using the one-personal-item and one-carry-on allowances and applying route, cabin, complimentary-bag benefits, and checked ordinal? Return zero for a carried or complimentary item.

inputs.name: bag_overweight_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in the same order, what overweight fee applies after using the standard weight allowance for that particular checked position, including any higher allowance limited to complimentary First or Business bags? Return zero where none applies.

inputs.name: bag_oversize_fees
inputs.question: For every current item in the same order, what oversize fee applies after adding its length, width, and height and selecting the current route's size band? Return zero where none applies.

skill.intent: Calculate the exact integer ticket price plus all current bag fees from aligned per-item base, overweight, and oversize assessments.

outputs.description: Exact integer ticket price plus all applicable fees for every current bag.
outputs.name: answer

premises.name: simultaneous_excess_rule

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

premises.question: When one checked bag is both overweight and oversize, which excess charge is added to its checked-bag fee?

fields.name: bag_base_fees

fields.name: bag_overweight_fees

reads.question: Jointly assess every current item under the itinerary's carried-item allowances, complimentary benefits, checked-bag ordinal schedule, weight rules, and total-dimension bands, returning aligned fee components.
reads.source_locator: current RuleArena Airline source_text, facts, and question

origin.quote: You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.

source_obligations.statement: Apply no more than one personal-item allowance and one carry-on allowance before assigning checked-bag positions.

origin.quote: 1st and 2nd checked bags are complimentary for:

source_obligations.statement: Apply cabin- and destination-based complimentary checked-bag benefits before using the successive checked-bag fee schedule.

origin.quote: The higher fee between oversize and overweight applies, in addition to the checked bag fee.

source_obligations.statement: For an item that is both overweight and oversize, add only the higher excess fee in addition to its base checked-bag fee.
